t: Subsection (a) of section 40 of said Act (Sec. 25–138, D. C. Code, 1940), as amended is hereby further amended by striking out the figures and word “50 cents” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$1”.

fable.w: This section only amends a dollar figure in an existing D.C. Code provision, changing "50 cents" to "$1". There is no tempting participation reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: by striking out the figures and word “50 cents” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$1”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple amendment to a fee or cost provision, changing a monetary amount from 50 cents to $1. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, public comment, advisory boards, or other forms of participation with parties outside the federal government. It is purely a legislative adjustment of a statutory figure.
qwen_block.s: Subsection (a) of section 40 of said Act (Sec. 25–138, D. C. Code, 1940), as amended is hereby further amended by striking out the figures and word “50 cents” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$1”.

opus.w: This section is a technical amendment that replaces "50 cents" with "$1" in a D.C. Code provision. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to consult on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision. The reference to the D.C. Code is only a citation and does not involve a local government in any decision.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** You might wonder whether a D.C. Code provision brings in a local government (the District of Columbia), which would be outside the federal government. That fails here. The amendment only changes a dollar amount from "50 cents" to "$1." Nobody is consulted, there's no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue, and no outside party takes part in any federal decision.
